title: One, Two, Three: Numbers You Can Hear
overview:
Count to twenty. Say it, then read it.
Answer the question: how many?
Say a phone number, one figure at a time.
Hear the difference between thirteen and thirty.
functions: Say a phone number one figure at a time
Hear the difference between thirteen and thirty
Read a number written as a figure
learningPath: Patterns: how many, and the -teen ending.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 4. Today, numbers.
You will hear numbers before you read them.
A price. A bus. A room. A phone.
So listen first.
One. Two. Three. Four. Five.
Say them with me. One. Two. Three. Four. Five.
Six. Seven. Eight. Nine. Ten.
Say them with me.
Now count to ten on your fingers.
After ten it changes. Listen.
Eleven. Twelve.
Those two are strange. Learn them alone.
Then it is easy again.
Thirteen. Fourteen. Fifteen. Sixteen.
Hear the end? Teen. Teen. Teen.
And after nineteen comes twenty.
Now the hard part. Listen well.
Thirteen. Thirty.
Thirteen is one three. Thirty is three tens.
The strong part moves. thir-TEEN. THIR-ty.
This one matters. It is money and time.
Last, a question. How many?
How many people? Three.
How many days? Seven.
Answer with a number. That is all.
That is Unit 4. Go and count.

grammar.title: One to twenty
grammar.explanation:
Ten numbers, then two strange ones.
Then it is easy again.
Learn them in three small groups.
grammar.rule:
1 one      2 two      3 three   4 four    5 five
6 six      7 seven    8 eight   9 nine    10 ten

11 eleven  12 twelve

13 thirteen  14 fourteen  15 fifteen
16 sixteen   17 seventeen 18 eighteen
19 nineteen  20 twenty
grammar.workedExample:
You want to say 16.
1. Is it under ten? No.
2. Is it eleven or twelve? No.
3. So take the small number: six.
4. Add teen: sixteen.
5. Say it: sixteen.
grammar.mistake:
Eleven and twelve do not follow the rule.
Do not say oneteen or twoteen.
Learn those two on their own.
grammar.tip: Thirteen to nineteen all end in teen.
grammar.practice:
Write the number.
1. five + one = ___
2. ten + one = ___
3. ten + three = ___
4. ten + ten = ___
5. nine + one = ___
grammar.answers:
1. six
2. eleven
3. thirteen
4. twenty
5. ten
All five? You can count to twenty.

grammar.title: Thirteen or thirty?
grammar.explanation:
These two sound alike and mean very different things.
It is money, time and buses.
The strong part tells you which.
grammar.rule:
thir-TEEN   (13)   the end is strong
THIR-ty     (30)   the start is strong

four-TEEN (14)  /  FOR-ty (40)
fif-TEEN (15)  /  FIF-ty (50)

Not sure? Ask: one three, or three zero?
grammar.workedExample:
A person says a price. You hear thirty or thirteen.
1. Listen to the strong part.
2. Strong at the end? It is thirteen.
3. Strong at the start? It is thirty.
4. Still not sure? Ask.
5. Say: One three, or three zero?
grammar.mistake:
Do not guess with money.
Asking costs nothing. Guessing costs money.
grammar.tip: Teen at the end is strong. Ty at the start is strong.
grammar.practice:
Which one?
1. THIR-ty
2. four-TEEN
3. FIF-ty
4. six-TEEN
5. SEV-en-ty
grammar.answers:
1. 30
2. 14
3. 50
4. 16
5. 70
Four or five right? Your ears are working.

grammar.title: How many?
grammar.explanation:
One question, and the answer is a number.
You will hear it every day.
grammar.rule:
How many people? Three.
How many days? Seven.
How many do you want? Two, please.

How many + thing + ?
Answer: just the number is enough.
grammar.workedExample:
You are in a shop. You want four.
1. They ask: How many?
2. You do not need a sentence.
3. Say the number: Four.
4. Add please: Four, please.
5. That is a complete answer.
grammar.mistake:
You do not have to make a long sentence.
A number alone is a good answer here.
grammar.practice:
Answer with a number.
1. How many days in a week?
2. How many months in a year?
3. How many fingers on one hand?
4. How many hands do you have?
grammar.answers:
1. Seven
2. Twelve
3. Five
4. Two
All four? You can answer how many.

grammar.title: Saying a phone number
grammar.explanation:
A phone number is not one big number.
It is figures, one at a time.
Zero is said zero or oh.
grammar.rule:
0 7 9 1 2 3 4
zero, seven, nine, one, two, three, four

Say them in small groups.
Stop after three or four figures.
Two the same? Say double: double four.
grammar.workedExample:
Your number is 0 7 7 1 2.
1. Start: zero.
2. Then seven.
3. Two sevens together: say double seven.
4. Then one, two.
5. Say it slowly, with a stop in the middle.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say the whole number fast.
Nobody can write that down.
Stop after three or four figures.
grammar.tip: Groups of three or four. Then stop.
grammar.practice:
Say these out loud.
1. 0 2 1
2. 5 5 6
3. 0 7 7 8
4. your own number
grammar.answers:
1. zero, two, one
2. five, five, six (or double five, six)
3. zero, seven, seven, eight (or zero, double seven, eight)
4. any correct reading
Check: did you stop in the middle?

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Count to twenty
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Say each group.
one two three four five
six seven eight nine ten
eleven twelve
thirteen fourteen fifteen
sixteen seventeen eighteen
nineteen twenty
Now record. Count from one to twenty.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: did you get eleven and twelve right?
speaking.tutor: Count to twenty with the tutor. Take one number each.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — How many?
speaking.instructions:
Listen to six questions. Answer with a number.
1. How many days in a week?
2. How many months in a year?
3. How many fingers on one hand?
4. How many eyes do you have?
5. How many letters in your name?
6. How many people in your home?
Tap the mic. Say six numbers.
Check: 1 seven, 2 twelve, 3 five, 4 two.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor four how many questions. Answer its questions too.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Thirteen or thirty?
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
thir-TEEN ... THIR-ty
four-TEEN ... FOR-ty
fif-TEEN ... FIF-ty
The teen words are strong at the end.
The ty words are strong at the start.
Now say these: 13, 30, 14, 40, 15, 50.
Tap the mic. Say all six.
Check: can you hear the difference yourself?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say thirteen or thirty. Say which one you heard.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Your age and your number
speaking.instructions:
Say four lines about yourself.
1. My name is (your name).
2. I am (your age) years old.
3. My phone number is (say the figures).
4. Stop in the middle of the number.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: could a person write your number down?
speaking.tutor: Say your phone number to the tutor. Ask it to read the number back.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Listen and write the number
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Write each number as a figure.
1.
2.
3.
4.
5.
6.
Now say them back out loud.
Check: 7, 12, 15, 20, 3, 18.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say five numbers. Write each one down.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Ask for a price
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Good morning. B: Good morning. How much is the bread?
2. A: One. B: And the milk?
3. A: Two. B: Two, please.
4. A: That is four. B: Sorry? Four or fourteen?
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did you ask when you were not sure?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor the price of three things. Check any price you did not hear.

writing.title: Writing 1 — The figures 0 to 20
writing.prompt:

writing.extension: Now write the words: one, two, three.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Numbers about you
writing.prompt:
Write four short lines about yourself.
Use a number in each one.
writing.model:

I have 2 children.
My room is number 9.
I work 8 hours.
writing.criteria:

A number in each one.
Each line starts with a capital.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Now write your phone number in figures.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Answer how many
activities.instructions:

activities.instructions:

quizzes.q: How many days are in a week?
How many months are in a year?
A shop says: How many? What is a good answer?
quizzes.why: How many wants a number. A number alone is enough.

quizzes.q: THIR-ty is strong at the start. Which number is it?
quizzes.why: Ty is strong at the start. Teen is strong at the end.

quizzes.q: four-TEEN is strong at the end. Which number is it?
quizzes.why: The teen ending means it is a number from 13 to 19.

quizzes.q: You did not hear the price. What do you say?
quizzes.why: Asking costs nothing. Guessing a price costs money.
0 is zero. In a phone number some people say oh.
Nineteen is the last teen. Then comes twenty.

quizzes.q: How do you say a phone number?
quizzes.why: Nobody can write down a number said that fast.

quizzes.q: Someone asks: How old are you? What do they want?
quizzes.why: How old asks for a number of years.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: Thirteen and thirty is the one that costs money
teacherNotes.note: It is the number mistake an adult actually makes, at a till and at a bus stop, and it is a listening problem rather than a counting one. Pattern 2 and Practice 3 are the heart of this unit. Teach the repair move too: one three, or three zero?

An adult meets a number spoken long before they meet it written — a price, a platform, a room, a phone. The lecture and Speaking 1 are deliberately ear-first, and the figures do not appear until Writing 1.

teacherNotes.type: Do not correct a phone number said slowly
teacherNotes.note: A learner who stops in the middle and says double seven is doing exactly the right thing, even if it sounds laboured. Speed comes later; being written down correctly is the point now.

teacherNotes.type: Eleven and twelve break the rule
teacherNotes.note: They are the only two that do, and a learner who says oneteen has understood the system and met an exception. Say that out loud rather than just correcting it.

assignment.title: Count, and say your number
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Count from one to twenty.
Then say your age and your phone number.
Stop in the middle of the number.
2. Write the figures 0 to 20 on a line.
Listen back before you finish. Could a person write your number down?
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
